intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the thrombopoietin gene (THPO; 600044) on chromosome 3q27.

checks.claim: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the thrombopoietin gene (THPO).
checks.evidence_quote: In conclusion, mutations of the THPO gene cause a form of CAMT that can be treated with THPO‐receptor agonists.
checks.explanation: Paper shows homozygous THPO p.R119C causes CAMT in a family; CAMT2 designation is nomenclature.

checks.claim: The THPO gene is located on chromosome 3q27.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome and targeted sequencing identified mutations in the gene encoding thrombopoietin (THPO)
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene the paper names. The abstract itself does not give 3q27.

paragraphs.text: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is an autosomal recessive bone marrow failure disorder. It begins with thrombocytopenia and a lack of megakaryocytes and can progress to pancytopenia and aplastic anemia. It is caused by loss of function of thrombopoietin, the ligand of the MPL receptor. Thrombopoietin is mainly made in the liver, so hematopoietic stem cell transplantation does not correct the defect. Patients have responded to thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as romiplostim.

checks.claim: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is an autosomal recessive bone marrow failure disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with recessive inheritance of the phenotype, the proband's siblings were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous for the variant
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance and bone marrow failure phenotype described.

checks.claim: CAMT2 begins with thrombocytopenia and a lack of megakaryocytes.
checks.evidence_quote: The disorder should be suspected in children or young adults presenting with hypo‐megakaryocytic thrombocytopenia with or without other peripheral cytopenias
checks.explanation: Thrombocytopenia with reduced megakaryocytes as the initial feature.

checks.claim: CAMT2 can progress to pancytopenia and aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: the oldest of the three affected siblings presented with trilineage bone marrow hypoplasia, while the younger ones had isolated thrombocytopenia or thrombocytopenia with anemia.
checks.explanation: Paper also notes the picture worsens with age and that it resembles CAMT with progression to aplasia.

checks.claim: CAMT2 is caused by loss of function of thrombopoietin.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, the R17C partial loss-of-function allele results in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state
checks.explanation: The disease is attributed to a partial loss-of-function THPO allele.

checks.claim: Thrombopoietin is the ligand of the MPL receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: Together with the recent identification of THPO receptor (MPL) mutations
checks.explanation: MPL is identified as the THPO receptor.

checks.claim: Thrombopoietin is mainly made in the liver.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering that thrombopoietin is mainly produced by the liver and other cells extrinsic to hematopoietic cells
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation does not correct the defect in CAMT2 because thrombopoietin is mainly made in the liver.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering that thrombopoietin is mainly produced by the liver and other cells extrinsic to hematopoietic cells, these patients are not expected to benefit from hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
checks.explanation: Stated directly, including the reasoning.

checks.claim: Patients with CAMT2 have responded to thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as romiplostim.
checks.evidence_quote: In all the three affected children, treatment with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim induced trilineage hematological responses, remission of bleeding and infections, and transfusion independence
checks.explanation: Response to romiplostim reported.

paragraphs.text: Dasouki et al. (2015) described a consanguineous Micronesian family in which several members had autosomal recessive aplastic anemia and pancytopenia.

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. described a consanguineous Micronesian family in which several members had aplastic anemia and pancytopenia.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing reveals a thrombopoietin ligand mutation in a Micronesian family with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
checks.explanation: The family is described as Micronesian, with 2 siblings who have aplastic anemia. The abstract does not say the family is consanguineous and does not mention pancytopenia.

checks.claim: The aplastic anemia and pancytopenia in the consanguineous Micronesian family described by Dasouki et al. showed autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently identified 2 siblings afflicted with idiopathic, autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
checks.explanation: The abstract states autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) reported patients with inherited bone marrow failure caused by THPO mutations. Their bone marrow failure did not respond to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, but blood counts improved with thrombopoietin receptor agonist treatment.

checks.claim: Seo et al. (2017) reported patients with inherited bone marrow failure caused by THPO mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We report 5 individuals in 3 unrelated families with severe thrombocytopenia progressing to trilineage bone marrow failure (BMF).
checks.explanation: The paper reports these patients with THPO mutations.

checks.claim: The bone marrow failure in the THPO-mutant patients reported by Seo et al. (2017) did not respond to hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
checks.evidence_quote: Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants and all showed poor graft function with persistent severe cytopenias even after repeated transplants with different donors.
checks.explanation: The transplanted patients' bone marrow failure did not respond to transplant.

checks.claim: Blood counts in the THPO-mutant patients reported by Seo et al. (2017) improved with thrombopoietin receptor agonist treatment.
checks.evidence_quote: For the 2 surviving patients, improvement in trilineage hematopoiesis was achieved following treatment with a THPO receptor agonist.
checks.explanation: Trilineage hematopoiesis improved after agonist treatment, which matches improved blood counts.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) reported children with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia due to a homozygous THPO mutation. Treatment with romiplostim was effective.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) reported children with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia due to a homozygous THPO mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a family with three children affected with CAMT caused by a homozygous mutation (p.R119C) of the THPO gene.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Romiplostim treatment was effective in the children with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia due to homozygous THPO mutation reported by Pecci et al. (2018).
checks.evidence_quote: In all the three affected children, treatment with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim induced trilineage hematological responses, remission of bleeding and infections, and transfusion independence, which were maintained after up to 6.5 years of observation.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of CAMT2 in the families reported by Dasouki et al. (2015) and later authors was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of CAMT2 in the family reported by Dasouki et al. was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently identified 2 siblings afflicted with idiopathic, autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
checks.explanation: The disorder in this family is described as autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of CAMT2 in families reported by authors after Dasouki et al. was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with recessive inheritance of the phenotype, the proband's siblings were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous for the variant
checks.explanation: This later family shows recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-1 (CAMT1) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the thrombopoietin receptor (MPL).

checks.claim: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-1 (CAMT1) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the thrombopoietin receptor (MPL).
checks.evidence_quote: The majority of CAMT cases are caused by biallelic mutations in the gene (MPL) encoding for the myeloproliferative leukemia virus oncogene (MPL) receptor, which abolish or severely impair the interaction of the receptor with its ligand thrombopoietin (THPO)
checks.explanation: MPL mutations cause CAMT; the CAMT1 label is nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Micronesian family with aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2015) used exome sequencing to identify a homozygous missense mutation in the THPO gene (R38C).

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. used exome sequencing in affected members of a consanguineous Micronesian family with aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
checks.explanation: Exome sequencing of the affected siblings is confirmed. The abstract does not say the family is consanguineous.

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. identified a homozygous missense mutation in the THPO gene (R38C) in affected members of a consanguineous Micronesian family with aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation encodes an arginine to cysteine substitution at residue 38 or residue 17 excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide
checks.explanation: The homozygous R38C missense mutation (also called R17C) is confirmed. The abstract does not say the family is consanguineous.

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) identified homozygous THPO mutations, including R99W, in patients with bone marrow failure.

checks.claim: Seo et al. (2017) identified homozygous THPO mutations in patients with bone marrow failure.
checks.evidence_quote: THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families, and THPO R157X, homozygous in the affected child in the third family.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous THPO mutations in patients with bone marrow failure.

checks.claim: The homozygous THPO mutations identified by Seo et al. (2017) in patients with bone marrow failure included R99W.
checks.evidence_quote: THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families
checks.explanation: R99W is one of the homozygous mutations reported.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) identified a homozygous THPO missense mutation in patients with CAMT who responded to romiplostim.

checks.claim: Pecci et al. (2018) identified a homozygous THPO missense mutation in patients with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia.
checks.evidence_quote: While no variants were found in MPL, we identified the homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C).
checks.explanation: Homozygous missense variant identified.

checks.claim: The patients with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia and a homozygous THPO missense mutation reported by Pecci et al. (2018) responded to romiplostim.
checks.evidence_quote: romiplostim was effective in increasing platelet count in all our patients, as well as in increasing hemoglobin concentration and neutrophil count in subjects presenting with anemia and/or neutropenia.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) and Pecci et al. (2018) found that thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as romiplostim improved hematopoiesis in patients with THPO mutations. In contrast, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation did not correct the defect, because thrombopoietin is produced outside the bone marrow.

checks.claim: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as romiplostim improved hematopoiesis in patients with THPO mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with our observations, trilineage response to romiplostim was achieved by two affected individuals homozygous for the p.R99W or p.R157* mutations of THPO (Seo et al, 2017).
checks.explanation: Trilineage response in this paper's patients and in Seo's patients.

checks.claim: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation did not correct the defect in patients with THPO mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: all showed poor graft function with persistent severe cytopenias even after repeated transplants with different donors
checks.explanation: Transplantation did not correct the defect.

checks.claim: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation does not correct the defect in patients with THPO mutations because thrombopoietin is produced outside the bone marrow.
checks.evidence_quote: Considering that thrombopoietin is mainly produced by the liver and other cells extrinsic to hematopoietic cells, these patients are not expected to benefit from hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
checks.explanation: The paper gives production outside hematopoietic cells as the reason.

clinical_synopsis.hpo_label: Bleeding with minor or no trauma

clinical_synopsis.feature: Reduced or absent bone marrow megakaryocytes

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Micronesian family with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2015) identified a homozygous arg38-to-cys (R38C) mutation in the THPO gene. The mutation was found by exome sequencing.

checks.claim: Dasouki et al. identified a homozygous arg38-to-cys (R38C) mutation in the THPO gene in affected members of a consanguineous Micronesian family with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation encodes an arginine to cysteine substitution at residue 38 or residue 17 excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide
checks.explanation: The homozygous R38C mutation in the affected siblings with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia is confirmed. The abstract does not say the family is consanguineous.

checks.claim: The THPO R38C mutation in the consanguineous Micronesian family was found by exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
checks.explanation: The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing.

paragraphs.text: Seo et al. (2017) identified a homozygous arg99-to-trp (R99W) mutation in the THPO gene in patients with inherited bone marrow failure.

checks.claim: Seo et al. (2017) identified a homozygous arg99-to-trp (R99W) mutation in the THPO gene in patients with inherited bone marrow failure.
checks.evidence_quote: THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous R99W mutation in affected patients.
